description: Eval scenarios for the building-timelines skill. Each case is a user prompt plus the grading flags grade-timeline.mjs should run with. Multi-track cases assert that the skill produces competitor/parallel swimlanes; single-track cases assert it does NOT over-impose lanes on a single narrative.

cases.prompt: Create a timeline of the AI LLM race with each key moment tracked, including model launches by key competitors.
cases.notes: The canonical case. Expect one swimlane per company (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek), models left→right, almost no intra-lane succeeded edges.

cases.prompt: Map the home video game console wars from the 1980s to today, tracking each manufacturer's console launches.
cases.notes: Expect lanes for Nintendo, Sega, Sony, Microsoft. Generations read as parallel rows, not one stacked block.

cases.prompt: Build a timeline of the web browser wars and each major browser's releases.
cases.notes: Expect lanes for Netscape/Mozilla, Microsoft (IE/Edge), Google (Chrome), Apple (Safari), Opera.

cases.prompt: Make a timeline of the Cold War space race between the US and USSR.
cases.notes: Two lanes (USA / USSR). Cross-lane edges for reactions (Sputnik caused NASA's founding) are good; per-lane succeeded chains are not.

cases.prompt: Map the founding and early scholarchs of the Stoic school in Athens.
cases.notes: A single tradition handed down — NOT multi-track. The skill should lean on the type lanes (people/events/periods) and succession edges, and should NOT invent company-style swimlanes. Run the grader WITHOUT --multi-track.

cases.prompt: Create a timeline of NASA's Apollo program from Apollo 1 to Apollo 17.
cases.notes: Single-narrative sequence. Lanes optional; grader run without --multi-track. Mainly tests richness (summaries, citations) and that a long sequence still reads cleanly (≤3 rows).
